description: Unfinished module the maker marks as work in progress: a wider Looper carrying the feedback control, the send and return, an arm input and clock and phase outputs on its own panel

params.text: Records on the first press, closes the loop and starts it playing on the second, and afterwards each press moves between playing and overdubbing
Clears the loop memory so a new loop can be recorded, and the cleared audio cannot be brought back
Stops recording and playback, and leaves the loop ready to play again from its beginning
Scales how much of the loop is written back on each pass, 0% to 100%, and the whole loop is written back whatever this reads while the looper is stopped
Nothing in the module reads this button except the lamp it toggles; audio at RETURN is written into the loop whenever a cable is patched there and the looper is not stopped
Balances the incoming signal against the loop: fully anticlockwise gives the incoming signal alone, the centre gives both at full level, fully clockwise gives the loop alone

inputs.text: A rising edge above 0V moves the looper to its next state in the order the large button follows: recording, then playing, then overdubbing
A rising edge above 0V stops recording and playback, and leaves the loop ready to play again from its beginning
A rising edge above 0V clears the whole loop memory; with a polyphonic cable each channel clears only the track of the same number
The left signal recorded into the loop and passed through to the left output; the number of channels here sets how many tracks the left side records
The right signal recorded into the loop and passed through to the right output; the number of channels here sets how many tracks the right side records
Moves the mix a fifth of its travel per volt and is added to the MIX knob
Nothing in the module reads this input except the lamp it lights, which stays lit until the next press of the large button
The left signal written into the loop in place of the loop's own audio, taken whenever a cable is patched here and the looper is not stopped
The right signal written into the loop in place of the loop's own audio, taken whenever a cable is patched here and the looper is not stopped
Adds a tenth of the feedback range per volt to the FEEDBACK knob, and the total is clamped between 0% and 100%

outputs.text: The left side of the loop mixed with the left input at the balance set by MIX, despite the tooltip naming it Clock
The right side of the loop mixed with the right input at the balance set by MIX, despite the tooltip naming it Phase
The left side of the loop as it is read out, before anything is written back, for feeding an effect
The right side of the loop as it is read out, before anything is written back, for feeding an effect
A 10V pulse each time the loop returns to its start
The position inside the loop, 0V at its start rising to 10V at its end

notes: there is no loop to play until one has been recorded. With the loop memory empty the large button starts recording, and ERASE puts the module back into that state
menu: Switching order — what the second press of the large button does: Record then Play then Overdub, or Record then Overdub then Play
Save audio with patch — On writes the loop memory to a file whenever the patch is saved, so the loop is there when the patch is opened again; Off leaves it unsaved
File settings — how an exported file is written: Format WAV or AIFF, Bit depth 16 bit or 24 bit, and Polyphony Sum or Multi-track
Export audio file — writes the loop memory to a file you name, and refuses while the loop memory is empty or while the looper is recording
